topics.topic: The Passion, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus Christ: Theological significance for humanity
learningObjectives: Analyze the Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem, Cleansing of the Temple, and the Last Supper
Examine the Agony in Gethsemane, betrayal by Judas, arrest, and trial before the Sanhedrin and Pilate
Evaluate the theological significance of Christ's sacrificial crucifixion, empty tomb, and bodily resurrection

topics.topic: The Great Commission and Ascension: Divine empowerment of the Church
learningObjectives: Analyze the post-resurrection appearances of Christ to Mary Magdalene and the eleven disciples
Examine the Great Commission (Matthew 28:18-20): global evangelism and making disciples
Describe the Ascension of Christ from Mount Olivet and the angel’s promise of the Second Coming (Parousia)

topics.topic: The Early Church: Day of Pentecost, Holy Spirit baptism, and communal fellowship (Acts 2)
learningObjectives: Detail the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost (wind, tongues of fire, glossolalia)
Analyze Peter’s maiden apologetic sermon citing Joel’s prophecy and the conversion of 3,000 souls
Examine the communal life of the early believers: apostolic teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers

topics.topic: Opposition and Persecution of the Early Church: Arrest of Peter and John, and Stephen’s martyrdom
learningObjectives: Examine the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate and subsequent arrest by Sadducees
Analyze Peter's bold declaration before the Council: 'We must obey God rather than men'
Trace the appointment of the seven deacons and the arrest, defense, and martyrdom of Stephen (Acts 6-7)

topics.topic: Spread of the Gospel Outside Jerusalem: Philip in Samaria, Ethiopian Eunuch, and Paul's conversion
learningObjectives: Analyze Philip's successful missionary campaign in Samaria and encounter with Simon Magus
Trace Philip's divine guidance to the Gaza road and baptism of the Ethiopian royal treasurer
Examine Saul of Tarsus's background, dramatic Damascus road conversion experience, and commissioning (Acts 9)

topics.topic: The Gentile Mission: Peter's vision at Joppa and baptism of Cornelius at Caesarea (Acts 10)
learningObjectives: Analyze Cornelius’s piety, angel encounter, and Peter’s trance on the rooftop in Joppa (sheet of animals)
Examine Peter's landmark revelation: 'Truly I understand that God shows no partiality'
Detail the Holy Spirit falling upon Gentiles and the defense of Gentile inclusion before the Jerusalem Church

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Acts of the Apostles Clinic
learningObjectives: Assess student mastery of the Resurrection, Pentecost, and the Gentile expansion of the Gospel
Conduct textual analysis of key passages in the Acts of the Apostles under examination timing
Remediate common historical and geographical misconceptions regarding apostolic journeys

topics.topic: The Jerusalem Council (Acts 15): Resolving the circumcision controversy for Gentile converts
learningObjectives: Identify the theological conflict instigated by Judaizers from Judea demanding circumcision for salvation
Analyze arguments presented by Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and James the brother of Jesus
Detail the historic Apostolic Decree and its liberating impact on the global expansion of Christianity

topics.topic: Paul's Missionary Journeys: Planting churches across Asia Minor, Macedonia, and Greece
learningObjectives: Trace Paul's first missionary journey with Barnabas (Cyprus, Perga, Antioch in Pisidia, Lystra)
Map Paul's second journey: the Macedonian call, Philippian jailer's conversion, and Mars Hill sermon in Athens
Trace the third journey, Ephesus riot, farewell to Ephesian elders at Miletus, and final arrest in Jerusalem

topics.topic: Justification by Faith: Teachings of Paul in Romans and Galatians
learningObjectives: Define justification as the divine act of declaring a sinner righteous through faith in Christ
Contrast justification through the works of the Mosaic Law versus justification by grace through faith
Use Abraham’s faith as the supreme Old Testament archetype of righteous imputation (Romans 4)

topics.topic: Christian Social Living: Love (1 Corinthians 13), humility (Philippians 2), and civic duties
learningObjectives: Examine Paul's sublime hymn on agape love: patient, kind, not envious, enduring all things
Explore the Christological hymn of humility and self-emptying (Kenosis) in Philippians 2:1-11
Apply apostolic ethical principles to marriage, master-servant relationships, and social responsibility

topics.topic: Comprehensive WASSCE/NECO CRS Revision & Past Question Marathon
learningObjectives: Review cumulative 3-year CRS syllabus covering Old Testament, Synoptic Gospels, Acts, and Pauline Epistles
Execute timed speed drills on 50 objective questions and complete 4 structured essay questions
Polish essay organization, biblical citations, and practical contemporary Nigerian applications

topics.topic: Terminal Mock Examination and Broadsheet Certification
learningObjectives: Administer comprehensive mock WASSCE CRS examination papers under strict invigilation
Score answer scripts in strict compliance with West African Examination Council criteria
Certify broadsheet records and finalize academic grading for graduation profiles
